definitions.explanation: Describes a situation or feeling that is extremely difficult to bear or tolerate. A literary, elevated expression.

examples.japanese: {忍|しの}び{難|がた}い⟦{苦|くる}しみ→苦しみ：14120_kurushimi⟧。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{屈辱|くつじょく}→屈辱：04853_kutsujoku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{忍|しの}び{難|がた}いもの⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: This humiliation is something truly hard to bear.

examples.japanese: ⟦{忍|しの}び→忍ぶ：16953_shinobu⟧{難|がた}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{忍|しの}び→忍ぶ：16953_shinobu⟧、⟦{耐|た}え→耐える：12087_taeru⟧{難|がた}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{耐|た}え→耐える：12087_taeru⟧。
examples.english: Enduring the unendurable, bearing the unbearable.
examples.notes: Famous phrase from Emperor Hirohito's 1945 radio address announcing Japan's surrender.

notes:
A literary compound adjective from ⟦{忍|しの}ぶ→忍ぶ：16953_shinobu⟧ (to endure) + ⟦{難|がた}い→難い：17198_gatai⟧ (difficult to). The pattern verb stem + ⟦{難|がた}い→難い：17198_gatai⟧ is productive in formal Japanese.

FAMOUS USAGE:
The phrase ⟦{忍|しの}び→忍ぶ：16953_shinobu⟧{難|がた}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{忍|しの}び→忍ぶ：16953_shinobu⟧ (⟦{耐|た}え→耐える：12087_taeru⟧{難|がた}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{耐|た}え→耐える：12087_taeru⟧) is one of the most famous lines in modern Japanese history, from Emperor Showa's radio broadcast on August 15, 1945, announcing Japan's acceptance of the Potsdam Declaration.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{耐|た}え{難|がた}い→耐え難い：19680_taegatai⟧: unbearable — near-synonym; focuses on endurance rather than patience
- ⟦{我慢|がまん}できない→我慢する：25343_gamansuru⟧: can't stand it — everyday equivalent; conversational
- {堪|た}えられない: unbearable — slightly more formal than ⟦{我慢|がまん}できない→我慢する：25343_gamansuru⟧
